chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about gypsum that is fired with dung and the bones of the dead, then the mosque is plastered with it: may one perform sajdah upon it?
So he عليه السلام wrote back to him in his own handwriting: “Indeed, the fire and the water have purified it.”

key_terms.أَيُسْجَدُ: whether sajdah may be performed on it
key_terms.النَّارَ: fire, described as part of the means of purification
key_terms.الْجِصِّ: gypsum or plaster used in construction
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: dung used here as fuel for firing the gypsum
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, described as part of the means of purification
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدُ: the mosque that is plastered with the material

ai.seo_question: Can one perform sajdah on mosque plaster made from gypsum fired with impure substances?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning plaster used in a mosque when it was processed through impure materials, including dung and the bones of the dead. Imam Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام states that fire and water have purified it, indicating the material may be used for sajdah after undergoing that transformation and purification.
